items.title: Uniform validity of the source query mode and spectral gap

source.anchor: S4.SS3.p2.1/p3.1; S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1-p1.2 and Px2.p2.1. Private actual-law numerical Ex23 component and Px2.p2.2.

source.scope: Numerical mode/gap prerequisite extracted from the original uniform source scalar regime, not Theorem4.1 or an oracle/TV/cost result.

items.statement: One natural dimension threshold makes the source mode and spectral gap valid uniformly over the original condition-number and integer query-cap range. \exists d_0(\delta)\ \forall d\ge d_0(\delta)\ \forall\kappa,q\text{ in the stated range}:\quad d\ge2,\qquad 1\le n=2q+1<d,\qquad d-n\ge\sqrt\kappa. Fix \(\delta\in\mathbb R\) with \(0<\delta<1\). The natural threshold is an existential output, chosen after this fixed parameter and before all dimensions, condition parameters and query caps. It depends only on \(\delta\). For every natural \(d\ge d_0(\delta)\), take a real \(\kappa\) with \(2\le\kappa\le d^{1-\delta}\), and a natural \(q\ge0\) satisfying \(q\le(\delta/256)\sqrt\kappa\log d\). The case \(q=0\) is included. Set \(n=2q+1\) as a natural number. In the gap inequality, dimension and mode are cast to the reals before subtraction. All powers with real exponents are standard real powers. The scalar \(q\) is the integer cap appearing in the source query regime. This numerical prerequisite does not define an algorithm, prove an oracle lower bound, or adapt expected cost to a deterministic worst-case cap. No TV precision or algorithmic conclusion is asserted. Dimension positivity, logarithm and real-power domains, mode range and the real gap are proved internally. No gap, asymptotic bound, threshold callback, moment or law certificate is an extra input.
